chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Umar was brought a woman who had been married to an old man. When he had copulated with her, he died upon her belly. So she gave birth to a child, but his sons claimed that she had committed fornication and testified against her. So Umar ordered that she be stoned.

Ali (peace be upon him) passed by her, so she said, 'O cousin of the Messenger of Allah! I have a proof.' He said, 'Bring me your proof.' So she handed him a letter, and he read it. He said, 'This woman is informing you of the day she was married, the day he copulated with her, and how their intercourse was. Return the woman!'

When it was the next day, he called for children of equal age and called the child (of the woman) along with them. He said to them, 'Play,' until the play distracted them. He said, 'Sit down.' When they had settled, he shouted at them. The children stood up, and the boy leaned on his palms. So Ali (peace be upon him) called him over, made him inherit from his father, and whipped his brothers who had falsely accused her, each receiving a legal penalty.
Umar said to him, 'How did you do this?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'I recognized the weakness of the old man in the boy leaning on his palms.'
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali use physical observation to prove a woman's chastity in a judicial case?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) mastery of *qiyas* (analogical reasoning) and empirical observation, specifically utilizing the physical sign of *istinkaf* (leaning on palms) to deduce the father's age and capacity for intercourse. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) where subtle physical evidence can overturn judicial presumptions, reinforcing the principle that the burden of proof lies with the accusers. The narrative serves as a classic example of how the Imams applied rational deduction to resolve complex family law disputes in the early Islamic community.
